component.name: Immich Folder Watch
component.summary: Upload media and synchronize local folders with Immich

description.p: Immich Folder Watch uploads photos and videos from local folders or synchronizes folders and albums with your Immich server in both directions. Choose a mode for each folder and control album mapping, file filters, transfer order, and logging. It runs as a per-user desktop app with X11 and XWayland support, talking to Immich over its public HTTP API rather than touching the server's storage directly.

An existing Immich server and an API key are required. Configure the connection after installation, then choose folders and grant access through the desktop folder picker. The linked help page explains setup.
Immich Folder Watch is a community desktop client maintained separately from the Immich project.

ul.li: Automatically upload screenshots into a dedicated Immich album.
Import existing photos and videos, then keep uploading new files.
Synchronize a local folder with one Immich album, including downloads.
Map first-level subfolders to Immich albums and keep media outside albums in the source root.
Per-folder modes for new-file uploads, existing and new uploads, or bidirectional synchronization.

Bidirectional sync propagates supported moves, renames, and deletions. Local deletions trash tracked Immich assets; assets removed from the remote source cause permanent deletion of tracked local files after a successful pull.
Optional album placement for uploads, single-album sync, or subfolders mapped to albums.
Per-folder extension and exclusion filters, with optional permanent local cleanup after verified uploads in upload modes.
Waits until files are fully written before upload; retries transient failures.
Remote change notifications via Socket.IO with polling fallback, plus connection and transfer status in the desktop interface.
Configurable upload/download order, batching, retries, logging, and start on login.
English and German UI with OS auto-detection and live language switching.

description.p: This major release requires migration for existing HTTP connections: use HTTPS or explicitly enable immich.allowInsecureHttp. Review the configuration and watch-root security documentation before upgrading installations that depend on linked folders or limited filesystem capabilities.

ul.li: Require HTTPS for Immich by default, with an explicit documented `allowInsecureHttp` migration option for trusted legacy HTTP installations.
Write Linux configuration containing API keys atomically with owner-only permissions; use a verified private directory for single-instance state.
Bound API response sizes and download resources, reject incomplete remote inventories before cleanup, and finalize downloads without replacing local files.
Refuse linked watch entries and scope folder-driven album mutations to newly created, explicitly recorded IDs; revoke folder authority after worker restarts and failed renames.

Pin watched directory identities and use retained file/directory handles for transfers, enumeration, cleanup, timestamp recovery and folder renames, preventing concurrent directory replacements from redirecting access.
Pin CI actions, the Flatpak build image and WinGet submission binary; restrict release job tokens and validate dispatcher tags outside executable source.

Signed GitHub Pages Flatpak repository for x86_64 and aarch64, with `.flatpakrepo`/`.flatpakref` installation, normal Flatpak updates, and release-triggered deployment alongside existing GitHub Release bundles.

Require supported secure filesystem primitives and reserve .ifw-internal- paths for protected transactions. Windows can block moves of active watch directories; Linux retains outer transaction containers after shutdown or cache eviction.
Retry a successful upload before later local cleanup after a restart or deletion failure; stored size and modification time alone no longer authorize deletion.
Updated the contributor workflow with maintained project/status records, automatic checkpoint guidance, and focused Codex agent profiles.
